limitations: Month-boundary effects: a typology instance whose burst straddles a month-end can be partially invisible to BOTH adjacent months' trailing-window evaluation (documented case: a rapid_movement instance spanning Aug31-Sep1 in the default dataset; confirmed to also affect FAN-02 - a January ring with 6 senders Jan23-29 and hub forward-outs Feb1-7 is invisible in BOTH January (outflows fall after month-end, excluded) and February (inflows fall before the 30-day lookback start, excluded)). This is a structural cost of point-in-time, no-future-leakage evaluation, not a bug - see scenarios.py.

FAN-01/FAN-02's tuning-period detection (0 of 17) looks alarming next to validation (2/17, 7/17) and test (2/11, 9/11), but is fully explained, not a bug: the 2 tuning-period rings are the dataset's worst-case instances - one is the month-boundary case above, the other has only 4 senders. The capacity constraint rules out any threshold loose enough to catch a 4-sender ring (min_hub_in_degree 3-4 produces 355-1046 alerts/month against a 200 cap, driven by the new legitimate pass-through look-alikes), leaving only min_hub_in_degree>=5 as capacity-feasible - which the 4-sender ring can never clear regardless of timing. Validation/test's 3 rings (6-7 senders each) aren't affected by either limitation. Verified directly against every grid point, not just the chosen one - see tuning_FAN-02.json's grid_results.

FAN-02's detection-rate numbers rest on only 5 labeled ring instances in the whole dataset. Any recovery ratio (e.g. 'X of 5 rings') should be read as a small, directional count, not a precise rate - with n=5, one more or fewer ring recovered swings the rate by 20 points. See ring_report for the per-ring, per-period breakdown (rings recovered vs. member recall) rather than reading detection_rate alone.

STR-01's test-period dip (4/8 vs. validation's 4/4) is a genuine threshold-generalization gap, not drift: the 4 missed test-period instances all have deposits spread across 7-10 days, which the chosen window_days=7 structurally cannot fully capture in any single 7-day slide. window_days=10 and 14 tie window_days=7 on validation (4/4 each, since validation's 4 cases all happened to be tightly spread) and score higher on tuning (23/28 vs 22/28); the tie-break toward minimum alert volume - defensible on its own, but under-informed with only 4 validation cases to discriminate on - picked the narrowest window, which doesn't generalize to wider-spread test-period bursts. A larger validation set would likely have broken the tie differently.
